pr_title: terminal: Fix non regex search to actually be non regex
pr_body:
Alacritty seems to support only regex search out of the box.
This PR just escapes all special regex chars to make non regex search work as expected.
Disclaimer: New to Rust.

Release Notes:

-Fixed [#4880](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/issues/4880).
pr_comments: Could someone have a look at the failed CI runs? Either it is lying or I just don't understand where this second import is coming from, because it's not where the compiler says it is.

While I also do not see the very same error when building, there's one definitely wrong thing: `std::collections::HashSet` usage per se — we're supposed to use `collections::HashSet` which is its own crate with an overidden hasher.
I merged https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/7481 and assume that rebasing on `main` would help with the compilation issues here.

> I merged #7481 and assume that rebasing on `main` would help with the compilation issues here.

It did, thanks.

>While I also do not see the very same error when building, there's one definitely wrong thing: std::collections::HashSet usage per se — we're supposed to use collections::HashSet which is its own crate with an overidden hasher.

Thanks for the info, but I decided to use a plain array instead of a HashSet after all. Both lookups are O(1) here and a simple test showed that searching an array of that size is faster than a lookup in the set. The code is also a bit simpler.

> I would really disagree with the `Both lookups are O(1) here` part

The array of special chars has a fixed length (independent of input, aka `n`), so a lookup is O(1), regardless of the data structure. If the size of the data structure were to depend on the input it would be O(n) for the array and O(1) for the map.
But maybe you meant all the lookups combined (which is O(n) for both - one lookup of O(1) for each input char).
@SomeoneToIgnore
Thank you for the elaboration, re-read it today with a fresh head — I think I was plain wrong when posted my original comment.
